experiments.name: load result combined with the base
experiments.notes: The load returns 32 bits, so the value has to be recombined with the base before it can be used as an address: this chain therefore always contains add.d (1 cycle, subtracted together with movfr2gr.s). The direct address chase that measures the 4-cycle bypass path for fld.d cannot be built for fld.s.

latencies.notes: 4 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. Unroll 6666, iters 1501. Raw measurement was 4.98; the residual is a systematic calibration offset, so the recorded value is the nominal integer with the observed spread.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024' --asm 'fld.s $f0, $r20, 0; fld.s $f1, $r20, 8; fld.s $f2, $r20, 16; fld.s $f3, $r20, 24; fld.s $f4, $r20, 32; fld.s $f5, $r20, 40; fld.s $f6, $r20, 48; fld.s $f7, $r20, 56'

notes: L1D-hit single-precision floating-point load: 5 cycles from the base address register to the loaded value through an ALU consumer, measured with movfr2gr.s (2 cycles) and add.d (1 cycle) in the chain. The 4-cycle bypass path that fld.d shows cannot be constructed here, because a 32-bit load result is never a complete 64-bit address (the chase would need a buffer below 2 GiB, and a low mmap made by the parent does not survive the exec into the benchmark). Within that limit the two widths behave identically: fld.s with the add.d reads 8.98 cycles against 8.94-8.98 for the same fld.d chain, so the 4/5 split of fld.d carries over and the difference between the two recorded numbers is the closure, not the hardware. Measured with --method slope, unroll 800/1600, on LA464 core 0. Re-derived with the two-cycle cross-domain calibration: movfr2gr and movgr2fr are 2 cycles each, movgr2frh.w is 3, the flag pair is 7/15, vpickve2gr is 3, xvpickve2gr is 5, and vreplgr2vr/xvreplgr2vr are 2 (3 for the byte and half-word broadcast).
